entities.summary:
Onatas was a Pythagorean philosopher who lived in or around the 5th century BC, possibly in either Croton or Tarentum in Magna Graecia. Nothing more is known about his life, but he is credited by Stobaeus as the author of a pseudonymous Neo-Pythagorean work from the 1st century BC or AD entitled On God and the Divine, which Stobaeus excerpts a long passage from.

The author of the passage ("Pseudo-Onatas") argues against the belief in a single deity, on the basis that the universe itself is not God but only divine, but that God is a governing part of the universe. Onatas was a philosophers & thinkers from Crotone. Recognized as a landmark figure with global significance (referenced in 0 Wikipedia editions). Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Onatas' philosophical work had a significant impact on Neo-Pythagorean thought, influencing later philosophers and thinkers in Magna Graecia. His ideas about the nature of God and the universe contributed to the development of Western philosophy.
